mission_02: wav2vec 2.0 is a self-supervised learning approach for speech recognition that learns powerful representations from raw audio without requiring transcriptions. The architecture consists of two main components: a convolutional feature encoder that processes raw waveform into a sequence of latent representations, and a Transformer encoder that produces contextualized representations. During pre-training, a portion of the latent representations are masked, and the model learns to predict which quantized codebook entry corresponds to each masked position through a contrastive loss. The convolutional encoder uses seven layers with stride 320 in the first layer and stride 1 in subsequent layers, progressively reducing the temporal resolution while increasing representational capacity. The contrastive objective compares the true codebook entry against distractor entries, encouraging the model to learn discriminative speech representations. A diversity loss encourages uniform utilization of the codebook entries. In this mission, you will implement the key components of wav2vec 2.0: the convolutional feature extractor, positional encoding, masked prediction loss with contrastive learning, and diversity loss for codebook utilization.
